title: Support and Integration of Family Units with Foreign Spouses
what_it_is: Support and Integration of Family Units with Foreign Spouses

sections.label: Support for transnational couples
sections.summary: MSF introduced the Marriage Preparation Programme and Marriage Support Programme in 2014 to help transnational couples integrate in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what support is given to family units comprising a foreign spouse in terms of integrating and entrenching themselves in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Therefore, in 2014, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) introduced the Marriage Preparation Programme (MPP) and Marriage Support Programme (MSP) to help these transnational couples.

sections.label: Programme reception and Friendship Programme
sections.summary: Over 98% of MPP and 97% of MSP participants reported the programmes helped, and a 2015 Friendship Programme matches volunteers to Non-Resident spouses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The programmes are well-received, with more than 98% of the MPP participants reporting that the programme has prepared them for marriage and that they could apply what they have learnt to their marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Similarly, more than 97% of the MSP participants said that the programme has helped Non-Resident spouses adjust to living in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In 2015, we also introduced the Friendship Programme, where a trained volunteer is matched to a Non-Resident spouse to help him or her integrate into Singapore.

sections.label: PA chit-chat sessions
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2018, PA organised 243 chit-chat sessions at Residents' and Neighbourhood Committees, reaching about 15,600 residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2018, PA organised 243 chit-chat sessions at Residents' Committees and Neighbourhood Committees, reaching out to about 15,600 residents.

sections.label: Employment and divorce rates
sections.summary: An average of 14,000 Non-Resident spouses with Long Term Visit Passes were employed yearly, and transnational divorce rates are comparable to Singaporean marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In terms of employment, over the past three years, an average of 14,000 Non-Resident spouses holding Long Term Visit Passes (LTVP/LTVP+) were employed in Singapore each year with a Letter of Consent issued by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The divorce rates for transnational marriages before the fifth and 10th year of their marriage anniversaries are comparable to those for Singaporean marriages from the same cohorts.

sections.label: Review of MPP and MSP
sections.summary: The Ministry is reviewing the MPP and MSP to find shortcomings and strengthen the programmes if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: My Ministry is in the midst of doing a review of the MPP and MSP to find out whether there are shortcomings in the programmes and, if there are, then we would want to strengthen them further.
